Czym jest „plaster” i jak łączą się częś: What is a grid panel, and how do the parts of the house connect?
Plaster to siatka krzyżujących się belek: A grid panel consists of crossing ribs, each made from a pair of boards. Placed horizontally, it forms a floor or ceiling; vertically, it forms a wall. End boards connect the panels: the side shortened by 24 cm rests on a full rib of the adjacent panel, while the longer side runs alongside it. This forms the wall-to-floor joint.

Belkę składamy z dwóch warstw desek. Prz: A beam is made from two layers of boards. One layer is offset along the other, so the end of one board sits beside an unbroken section of its neighbour. Add more boards to extend the beam.
Wsuwamy belki w siebie pod kątem 90°. Wp: Slide the beams together at 90°. Each slot reaches halfway through the beam height, so the joint stays within the height of one beam. This creates a grid panel of ribs and open cells.
Plastry układamy poziomo jako podłogę i: Grid panels form floors and ceilings when laid horizontally, and walls when placed vertically. The roof uses the same grid. Adjacent panels connect through slots and stepped board ends.
Do komór podłogi, ścian zewnętrznych i d: Fitted insulation blocks go into the cells of the floor, external walls and roof. Membranes, linings and finishes follow. The facade covers the structure shown in this model.
